concerns.text: User Story US4 (Privacy Auditing) has no associated Success Criteria. All other user stories are linked to at least one SC (e.g., SC-002 for US1, SC-001 & SC-009 for US2, SC-003 for US3). The absence of a success criterion for US4 leaves the story under‑specified and provides no measurable target for the privacy audit requirement (FR-005).

Duplicate functional requirement identifier **FR-001** appears in the Spec Template placeholder list (under “## Requirements” → “### Functional Requirements”) while a concrete FR-001 is already defined in the Functional Requirements section. This creates ambiguity about which definition is authoritative.

Functional requirement identifier FR-001 is defined twice (once in the main Functional Requirements section and again in the Spec Template placeholder list). Duplicate IDs create ambiguity about which definition is authoritative, making verification of the requirement impossible until the conflict is resolved.

Success Criterion SC-002 requires the cleaned dataset to contain ≥ 150 records after exclusions. Given the ADReSS dataset size (~170 total) and the documented exclusion rules (missing labels, < 50 words), it may be impossible to meet this threshold, rendering the criterion potentially unreachable and untestable.

FR-002 specifies ANCOVA with age and education as covariates, yet the reporting requirements (FR-002 & FR-003) call for Cohen's d effect sizes with 95 % confidence intervals. Cohen's d is a raw, unadjusted standardized mean difference appropriate for simple t‑tests, not for ANCOVA-adjusted group comparisons. Using an unadjusted d after covariate adjustment creates a mismatch between the statistical model and the effect‑size metric, potentially misrepresenting the magnitude of group differences.

new_concerns.text: The Spec Template section re‑introduces placeholder functional requirements (FR-001 … FR-005) that duplicate the concrete FR identifiers defined earlier. These placeholder FRs have no story anchors, creating identifier collisions and orphaned requirements.

FR-007 specifies an a priori power analysis targeting a medium effect size expressed as Cohen’s d (d = 0.5), yet the primary statistical test is ANCOVA with effect sizes reported as partial eta‑squared (η²). Using Cohen’s d for power calculations is mismatched to the ANCOVA framework and may produce inaccurate power estimates for the planned analyses.
